text: BOMBSHELL IN CANTON POLITICS.

label: text
text: EFFECT ON BOYCOTT.

label: text
text: What Does Chang Kai-shek Mean?

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Canton, Jüne 1.

label: text
text: Dr. C. C. Wu, mayor of Canton, holder of many important committee positions under the Kuomintang Government, left Canton secretly last night, en route for Hongkong, and is bound for Shanghai, nominally on a "month's leave of absence."

label: text
text: When his departure becomes known in Canton (to-night it is still a semi-official secret) it will strike consternation into the heart of the moderates, coming, as it does, close upon the heels of the news of the arbitrary arrest on Sunday of General Wu Te-chen, formerly Canton's chief of police. Indeed it is surmised in many circles that Dr. C. C. Wu's abrupt departure is not entirely disconnected with General Chang Kai-shek's arrest of Wu Te-chen, who today was transferred from the city to the military prison at Whampoa.

label: text
text: In real importance Dr. Wu's departure overshadows even the resolutions passed this morning by the Military Council which direct the civil government as follows:—

label: text
text: “All departments concerned are instructed to open negotiations at once for the speedy ending of the Hongkong-Canton strike and boycott.”

label: text
text: "The oil monopoly shall be brought to an end on June 16."

label: paragraph_title
text: Extreme Significance.

label: text
text: These two bare official resolutions are fraught with extreme significance, but whether they will bring about a termination of strained trade and diplomatic relations depends entirely upon whether other officials follow Dr. C. C. Wu's precedent of abrupt and secret departure, and, if they do so, on the political complexions of the men chosen to succeed them.

label: text
text: For the immediate present Chen Yun-tong, chief secretary of the mayor's office, is carrying on as "acting mayor," but it is understood that a new man will soon be named.

label: text
text: Apparently General Chang Kai-shek is assuming all the powers of a military dictator, and changing at will civil appointments and civil officials. How long this will be endured by order-loving Kuomintang members who have striven against Communism cannot be foretold.

label: text
text: It is considered extremely doubtful if the importing companies will pay this tax. The present tax, on kerosene, is already $4 a case, but the Government will contend that the need of war revenue will necessitate an increase in the tax since the monopoly and attendant profits are being sacrificed.

label: text
text: With regard to the oil monopoly resolution it seems that the Government is going to increase greatly the tax against which oil importers have already protested as a violation of treaty obligations.

label: text
text: “Oil” From Oil.

label: text
text: Wu Te-chen, it is learned, had feared that his position here was becoming untenable, and had planned to depart late this month for a long tour of the United States.

label: text
text: While their general is in prison, Wu Te-chen's troops are being disarmed. They possessed the finest machine-gun equipment in South China.

label: text
text: The Chang. Kal-shek forces are also receiving other war supplies in the form of nine military aeroplanes, shipped from Russia, which will arrive late this week. These "planes are equipped with bombing apparatus, machine-guns and other accessories, and officers paid by the Russia Soviet are said to be accompanying them.

label: text
text: The House of Commons, 31st楼 (2023) votes to 100, carried an address of thanks to His Majesty for the proclamation continuing the Emergency Regulations, including a new regulation empowering the Home Secretary to prohibit a Bank or private individuals dealing in moneys or securities imported from abroad intended to be applied to any purpose "prejudicial to the public safety or life of the community."

label: text
text: The Labourites, headed by Mr. Ramsay MacDonald, contended that the Regulations were now unnecessary in view of the good conduct of the people during the strike.

label: text
text: The Tenth Division of the Fourth Army has also been ordered north, and 800 troops have arrived from Hoihow on the steamer "Hoi Hung." The steamers "Piave," "Huihoi" and "Heijung" are busy carrying troops from Hoihow to Kongmoon.

label: paragraph_title
text: Crack Regiments

label: text
text: The Second, Fourth and Tenth regiments of the First Revolutionary Army, General Chang Kai-shek's crack troops, have received orders from the general himself to proceed north and to become the nucleus of the new First Division of the Northern Expedition. General Wang Pahlin, commander of the Twentieth Division, has been named new commander of this new First Division, and has also started north by rail with his command.

label: text
text: As soon as local affairs are more composed, General Chang Kai-shek will himself go to the northern front. Great anxiety is manifested here as to whom he may name for the local military command during his absence.

label: text
text: The Political Training Department of the Kuomintang Military Committee, will also soon take to the field under the direction of Chen Pong-kok, chairman of the department. One thousand canvas beds and 1,000 mosquito nets have been ordered for these propaganda workers alone.

text: General Chan Cheung-po has arrived with troops from Yeung-kong, to perform garrison duty at Kongmoon and Pakkai, other detachments having been withdrawn to Canton to embark with the Northern Expedition.

label: text

label: text
text: Canton, June 1

label: text
text:
Additional details from the gunpowder works' explosion at Whampoa on Sunday increase rather than diminish the seriousness of the disaster. In all ten persons lost their lives, and 116 injured have been accounted for, of whom six were soldier patients in the Whampoa Military Hospital. They were injured by flying fragments, and the roofs of houses more than two miles from the scene of the explosion were wrecked by falling debris.
Ping Kong, the Whampoa suburb in which the explosion occurred, has been closed to traffic and to all except the military.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: HAPPY VALLEY PARADE.

label: text
text: The added attractiveness of a parade visible to all in comfort and affording opportunity for full effect was responsible for thousands visiting Happy Valley this morning, even the extra arrangements by the Tramway Company proving inadequate to cope with the crowds of could-be travellers.

label: text
text: From before 8.30 a.m. onwards every tram travelling eastward was packed to its utmost capacity and groups were left at each stopping place. A steady stream of cars, ricshas and pedestrians was observed the whole Way.

label: text

label: text

label: text
text: To-night's Reception.

label: text
text:
Some fourteen hundred guests are expected at the reception at Government House to night. The proceedings are to be as informal as possible, the rooms and grounds having been laid out with a view to achieving this. There will be dancing to a string orchestra for those who wish and the brass band of the East Surreys is to discourse music from the grounds, the veranda, the provided plenty of sitting out accommodation.
The grounds have been illuminated and decorated in accordance with the scheme prevailing throughout the rooms in the house, this being entirely Chinese, a change from the greenery effects usually associated with previous Birthday.

label: text
text: London, June 21

label: text
text: A brief gable from Malta announcing that the battleship Resolution, with Rear-Admiral Staveley, has been ordered to Egypt forthwith, coincides with recent indications that the Cabinet, however preoccupied with the coal problem, is now grappling with a very delicate situation in Egypt, where the Zaghulista's return to power by a sweeping majority as the result of the elections has been followed by the news that Zaghul Pasha maintains his former uncompromising attitude, declining to accept the British reservations in regard to the control of the Soudan, safeguarding the Suez Canal, the protection of foreign interests in Egypt, and the defence of that country.

label: text
text: A sensation has been caused by the resignation of Judge—President Kershaw, who, with two Egyptian judges, pronounced the verdict in the conspiracy trial, on the ground that the verdict in the case of four of the accused was contrary to the weight of evidence and constituted a grave miscarriage of justice.

label: text
text: His Majesty's Government today addressed a Note to the Egyptian Government in this connection reserving judgment in respect of the verdict, which it meanwhile declines to accept as proof of the accused men's innocence and also reserving full liberty of action in the matter.

Judgment as regards the other accused will be announced on May 25.—On May 25 a cable stated: The conspiracy trial resulted in all accused being acquitted, except Fahmy Ali Beal, who was sentenced to death.]

Canton, June 1.
In spite of disturbed conditions across the creek, the residents of Shameen are making enthusiastic preparations for the observance of June 3, the birthday anniversary of King George.
At 9.30 a.m. there will be a dress parade of the sailors and soldiers of His Majesty stationed on or near Shameen. This will be followed by special services at 11 a.m. at Christ Church, and at 11:30 there will be a formal reception at the Canton Club in Shameen, where a ball will also be given for the evening. If possible a programme of outdoor sports will be arranged for the afternoon.

label: text
text: Canton, May 31

label: text
text: Four Japanese were arrested today at a Hotel in Honam, charged with assisting Chinese to reach the Hongkong steamer. Three of them are now in the Strikers' Prison, and one is in the City. Jail. The Japanese Consul has protested.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text:
Pakkai, Kongmoon; May 16.
The U.S.S. "Pampanga" arrived this afternoon and left next morning. She brought a foreign gentleman representing the Texas Oil Co., who is to take up with the Kerosene Monopoly, the matter of the seizure of 2,000 cases of the company's oil, from their godown, a week ago. The cargo has been sent to Canton by order of the Canton Commercial Bureau. The Texaco man subsequently left for Canton as well.

label: text
text: A sailor employed on the Chinese Customs launch at Gaemoon station has been kidnapped by pirates, for ransom.

label: text
text: May 19.

label: text
text: It is alleged that local steam-launches, which fly foreign flags (under foreign registry "for protection"), also put up Chinese Naval ensigns, when passing this port, so as to avoid reporting to the Customs. The Commissioner of Customs has ordered all vessels under foreign registry to present papers to the general office for examination.

label: text
text: The Pakkai Presbyterian mission hospital continues to function under the protection of the mayor of Kongmoon.

label: text
text: May 25.

label: text
text: The Sunning Railway has imported coal from Canton, this arriving in several junks. Because the Tung Tak (cargo coolies on land) and the Chap Yin (shore and ship coolies) guilds have been disputing for the right of discharging the coal, the junks proceeded to Kungyick instead of coming here. This morning the train had no coal and used firewood instead.

label: text
text: The former Hongkong steamer "San Ning" will ply between this port and Canton a week hence.

label: paragraph_title
text: Agitators Jeered

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Canton, June 1.

label: text
text:
Signs are not wanting here that the general populace is becoming weary of the reiteration of meaningless catchwords which have been popular in the past. At 7 o'clock on Sunday evening, two revolutionary speakers took the platform at the Lok Tin Theatre in the west end, and began long harangués about "imperialism" and about the Shanghai shootings of last year. They were jeered and hooted into silence by the crowd, which was anxious for the cinema programme to begin.
Charterless and illegal unions have been warned by the Government that they will be severely penalised for molesting Chinese or foreigners on the pretext of picket duty. Offences of this kind, accompanied by virtual blackmail, have been growing more and more numerous.
